best_plan.name: p1
best_plan.rationale: p1 is the best observed trade-off: it uses an exact row filter on the movie slug and projects down to only reviewId and reviewText before the single semantic step, then scores sentiment with Gemini Flash Lite. Among executed plans, it achieved the highest quality (spearman_correlation about 0.774) while also having the lowest cost (about $0.0271); p2 was both slower and slightly more expensive with worse quality, and p3 was slightly faster wall-clock but costlier and lower quality.

cost_model_explanation: The cost model was updated from simple priors to an empirical per-operator model using observed traces, and it consistently showed that sem_map dominated both dollar cost and latency while exact filter and project were effectively free. That pushed plan design toward doing all exact pruning first and keeping only the review text for the LLM. In observed runs, Gemini Flash Lite was the cheapest effective semantic mapper and delivered better quality than the nano alternative for this task.

plan_codes.p1:
pipeline = PhysicalPipeline(plan_name, "Reviews.csv", load_data("Reviews.csv"))
pipeline.filter(lambda row: str(row.get("idx", "")).strip() == "ant_man_and_the_wasp_quantumania")
pipeline.project(["reviewId", "reviewText"])
pipeline.sem_map(
    [{
        "name": "score",
        "type": int,
        "description": "Based only on the review text, assign an integer score from 1 to 5 for how much the reviewer liked the movie: 1=strongly disliked, 2=mostly negative, 3=mixed or neutral, 4=mostly positive, 5=strongly liked."
    }],
    model=pz.Model.GOOGLE_GEMINI_2_5_FLASH_LITE,
    depends_on=["reviewText"]
)
pipeline.project(["reviewId", "score"])
pipeline
